graph_state: empty (genesis — authored fresh from scholarship, no DB access)

nodes.name: Honesty
nodes.conduct: the disposition not to mislead — about data, methods, or yourself
frontiers: differentiate: honesty toward others vs. honesty with oneself

nodes.name: Rigor
nodes.conduct: the disposition to subject claims to the severest available test
nodes.basis: Kuhn theory-choice virtues (accuracy, consistency); Mayo severe testing
frontiers: differentiate: rigor of measurement vs. rigor of inference

nodes.name: Care
nodes.conduct: the disposition to attend to those affected by the inquiry
frontiers: differentiate: care for participants vs. care for downstream users of the result

nodes.name: Courage
nodes.conduct: the disposition to bear cost for the sake of the inquiry
frontiers: differentiate: courage against the field vs. courage against one's own past self

nodes.name: Openness
nodes.conduct: the disposition to make the work available to scrutiny and reuse
frontiers: differentiate: openness of artifacts vs. openness of reasoning

nodes.name: Humility
nodes.conduct: the disposition to track the limits of what one knows
nodes.basis: Baehr, The Inquiring Mind; intellectual humility literature
frontiers: differentiate: humility about evidence vs. humility about standing to speak

nodes.name: Justice
nodes.conduct: the disposition to distribute epistemic credit and burden fairly
nodes.basis: Fricker, epistemic injustice; Longino on social knowledge
frontiers: differentiate: testimonial vs. hermeneutical justice in research practice

nodes.name: Autonomy
nodes.conduct: the disposition to let evidence, not incentive, govern the question
nodes.basis: Merton organized skepticism; Longino on independence of judgment
frontiers: differentiate: autonomy from funders vs. autonomy from disciplinary fashion

nodes.name: Reporting null and disconfirming results
nodes.conduct: when the data refuse your favored hypothesis, you write them up as prominently as you would a confirmation
frontiers: differentiate: nulls in confirmatory vs. exploratory designs

nodes.name: Owning the load-bearing assumption
nodes.conduct: you name the single assumption your result depends on, and state what breaks if it is false, before a reviewer finds it
nodes.basis: Douglas on inductive risk; intellectual-humility literature
frontiers: differentiate: assumptions you can test now vs. assumptions you defer

nodes.name: Sharing the messy pipeline, not just the clean result
nodes.conduct: you release the analysis with its dead ends and judgment calls intact, not a sanitized rerun built for the camera
frontiers: differentiate: disclosing process vs. disclosing artifacts

nodes.name: Crediting the unseen labor
nodes.conduct: you name the technician, student, or community whose work the result rests on in author position, not a footnote
frontiers: differentiate: visible co-authors vs. structurally invisible contributors

nodes.name: Auditing your own method for the failure you'd hate to find
nodes.conduct: you run the analysis designed to break your conclusion, not the one that flatters it
frontiers: differentiate: internal robustness checks vs. inviting external attack

nodes.name: Calibrating confidence to evidence
nodes.conduct: your stated certainty in the abstract tracks the strength of the actual test, not the importance of the claim
frontiers: differentiate: calibration of point estimates vs. of scope conditions

nodes.name: Protecting the vulnerable participant beyond the consent form
nodes.conduct: you weigh harms the IRB checkbox doesn't cover and stop a procedure that is technically permitted but wrong
frontiers: differentiate: individual harm vs. collective/community harm

nodes.name: Pursuing the question that won't fund itself
nodes.conduct: you commit to the problem the field considers unfashionable because the evidence, not the incentive, points there
nodes.basis: Merton organized skepticism; Polanyi on independent inquiry
frontiers: differentiate: career-risk questions vs. funding-structure-orphaned questions

nodes.name: Letting the anomaly redirect the program
nodes.conduct: when a stray result contradicts the framework you built a career on, you follow it instead of explaining it away
nodes.basis: Kuhn on anomaly; Longino on accommodating dissent
frontiers: differentiate: anomaly from others vs. anomaly in your own replication

nodes.name: Making the work reproducible by a stranger
nodes.conduct: you write the methods so a competitor with no access to you could rebuild the result from scratch
frontiers: differentiate: computational reproducibility vs. methodological replicability

nodes.name: Centering the knowledge the discipline overlooks
nodes.conduct: you treat practitioner and indigenous accounts as evidence to be tested, not anecdote to be displaced
nodes.basis: Fricker epistemic injustice; Haraway situated knowledge
frontiers: differentiate: admitting overlooked evidence vs. sharing back with its source

nodes.name: Choosing the simpler model only when it pays its way
nodes.conduct: you adopt the leaner explanation when it predicts as well, and you say so when you kept complexity only to fit data you already saw
frontiers: differentiate: parsimony as predictive virtue vs. parsimony as honesty about overfitting

nodes.name: Disclosing a null that undercuts your own prior published claim
nodes.conduct: you flag, in the new paper, that the null reverses something you previously asserted in print
frontiers: someone find this: self-retraction-via-new-evidence cases

nodes.name: Publishing a finding that sinks your grant-renewal story
nodes.conduct: you report the disconfirming result even though it weakens the narrative your next funding round depends on
frontiers: differentiate: funding cost vs. reputational cost of the null

nodes.name: Pre-committing to report whatever the outcome
nodes.conduct: you register the analysis plan and the intent to publish before seeing the data, removing the option to bury a null
parent_paths: Making the work reproducible by a stranger
frontiers: differentiate: pre-registration vs. registered report as commitment devices

nodes.name: Naming the assumption that, if false, reverses the conclusion
nodes.conduct: you isolate the one premise whose failure would flip the result, and you state it explicitly in the paper
frontiers: differentiate: load-bearing modeling vs. measurement assumptions

nodes.name: Flagging the assumption you currently cannot test
nodes.conduct: you mark, as an open limit, the premise you are relying on but have no present means to check
frontiers: someone find this: papers that flag untestable premises as standing limits

nodes.name: Releasing raw data with the cleaning steps logged
nodes.conduct: you publish the unprocessed data alongside an auditable record of every exclusion and transformation
parent_paths: Sharing the messy pipeline, not just the clean result
frontiers: differentiate: raw-data release vs. provenance-trail release

nodes.name: Reporting the analyses you ran and discarded
nodes.conduct: you list the specifications you tried and dropped, so readers can see the garden of forking paths you walked
parent_paths: Sharing the messy pipeline, not just the clean result
frontiers: differentiate: disclosing discarded analyses vs. reporting a full multiverse

nodes.name: Naming the technician in author position, not acknowledgments
nodes.conduct: you move the person who built the apparatus or ran the assays into authorship where their work warrants it
frontiers: differentiate: technical labor vs. interpretive labor in credit allocation

nodes.name: Co-authoring with the community whose knowledge you used
nodes.conduct: you bring the source community into authorship and analysis rather than mining them for data and moving on
parent_paths: Centering the knowledge the discipline overlooks
nodes.basis: Haraway situated knowledge; community-based participatory research
frontiers: someone find this: co-authorship with non-academic knowledge-holders

nodes.name: Running the robustness check most likely to overturn the headline
nodes.conduct: you choose the stress test that would most embarrass your main claim, and report it whichever way it falls
parent_paths: Auditing your own method for the failure you'd hate to find
frontiers: differentiate: specification robustness vs. data-perturbation robustness

nodes.name: Inviting an adversarial collaborator to attack the design
nodes.conduct: you recruit a skeptic of your hypothesis into the study so the protocol survives a hostile reading before it runs
parent_paths: Auditing your own method for the failure you'd hate to find
frontiers: someone find this: documented adversarial-collaboration designs

nodes.name: Treating a replication failure of your own work as signal
nodes.conduct: when your own result fails to replicate, you investigate it as information rather than defending the original
parent_paths: Letting the anomaly redirect the program
Auditing your own method for the failure you'd hate to find
frontiers: differentiate: failed self-replication vs. failed independent replication

nodes.name: Inviting the rival explanation into your own paper
nodes.conduct: you build the strongest competing account of your data into your own discussion and test it head-to-head
parent_paths: Letting the anomaly redirect the program
Auditing your own method for the failure you'd hate to find
nodes.basis: strong inference; Longino on accommodating critique
frontiers: differentiate: steelmanning rivals vs. formal model comparison

nodes.name: Widening error bars to include model uncertainty, not just sampling noise
nodes.conduct: your reported uncertainty absorbs the choice of model and analyst, not only the variance within one fixed model
frontiers: differentiate: model uncertainty vs. analyst (many-analysts) uncertainty

nodes.name: Stating the conditions under which you'd be wrong
nodes.conduct: you specify in advance the observations that would defeat your claim, not just the ones that would support it
frontiers: differentiate: defeating evidence vs. scope-limiting conditions

nodes.name: Refusing to overclaim significance you didn't pre-specify
nodes.conduct: you present a post-hoc finding as exploratory, declining to dress it in confirmatory language
frontiers: someone find this: papers that label findings exploratory at cost to impact

nodes.name: Abandoning a framework you are known for when it fails a clean test
nodes.conduct: you retire the theory your reputation rests on once it loses a decisive, pre-specified test
parent_paths: Letting the anomaly redirect the program
frontiers: differentiate: abandoning vs. publicly revising a signature framework

nodes.name: Stopping a permitted procedure that is causing distress
nodes.conduct: you halt a study step that participants are tolerating but visibly suffering, even though consent technically covers it
parent_paths: Protecting the vulnerable participant beyond the consent form
nodes.basis: ethics of care; beneficence beyond compliance
frontiers: differentiate: acute distress vs. cumulative burden as stopping triggers

nodes.name: Refusing a design that extracts from a community without return
nodes.conduct: you decline a study that takes data or samples from a community and gives nothing back to them
parent_paths: Protecting the vulnerable participant beyond the consent form
frontiers: someone find this: refusals or redesigns on extraction grounds

nodes.name: Continuing a line your senior collaborators have written off
nodes.conduct: you keep pursuing a result your advisors and co-authors have declared a dead end, because the evidence isn't settled
parent_paths: Pursuing the question that won't fund itself
nodes.basis: intellectual courage; hierarchy and dissent in labs
frontiers: differentiate: dissent within a lab vs. dissent against the field

nodes.name: Declining the fundable reframing that distorts the question
nodes.conduct: you turn down the grant-friendly framing that would bend the inquiry away from what you actually want to know
parent_paths: Pursuing the question that won't fund itself
frontiers: someone find this: documented refusals of distorting reframings

nodes.name: Specifying every parameter a reanalysis would need
nodes.conduct: you report seeds, versions, and settings so a reanalyst needs nothing from you to reproduce the numbers
parent_paths: Making the work reproducible by a stranger
frontiers: differentiate: parameter completeness vs. environment completeness

nodes.name: Sharing code and environment, not just describing them
nodes.conduct: you ship the runnable code and a captured environment, rather than a prose description a reader must reconstruct
parent_paths: Making the work reproducible by a stranger
Making the work reproducible by a stranger
frontiers: differentiate: code release vs. full environment capture

nodes.name: Publishing in the language and venue the source community can access
nodes.conduct: you make the findings reachable to the people studied, not only to the journal's paywalled readership
parent_paths: Centering the knowledge the discipline overlooks
frontiers: someone find this: parallel community-facing publication of findings

nodes.name: Penalizing added parameters against out-of-sample prediction
nodes.conduct: you keep a parameter only if it improves prediction on data you hadn't seen, not the fit on data you had
parent_paths: Choosing the simpler model only when it pays its way
frontiers: differentiate: cross-validation vs. information-criterion penalties

nodes.name: Admitting when complexity was added post hoc to fit observed data
nodes.conduct: you disclose that an extra term was introduced after seeing the data, rather than presenting it as principled a priori
parent_paths: Choosing the simpler model only when it pays its way
frontiers: someone find this: explicit disclosures of post-hoc model complexity
